questions.q: What is the main advantage of a slicer over a PivotTable's built-in field dropdown filter?
options: The current filter state is always visible as highlighted buttons, instead of being hidden behind a dropdown arrow
Slicers can only be used with numeric fields, which makes them more precise
Slicers eliminate the need for a PivotTable entirely
There is no real advantage — they behave identically
questions.explain: A slicer shows every possible value as an always-visible button with selected values highlighted, so anyone looking at the report can see the current filter state without clicking anything.

questions.q: What happens when you check multiple fields in the Insert Slicers dialog?
options: A separate slicer is created for each checked field, all in one step
Only the first checked field gets a slicer
Excel merges all checked fields into a single combined slicer
The dialog only allows checking one field at a time
questions.explain: The Insert Slicers dialog lists every available field as a checkbox, and checking several creates one slicer for each field in a single step.

questions.q: Why does Excel offer a separate Timeline control instead of just using a regular slicer on a date field?
options: A regular slicer would list every individual date as its own button, which is unusable across a dataset spanning years — a Timeline instead offers a drag-to-select range with a zoomable granularity
Timelines and slicers are actually the exact same feature under two different names
Regular slicers cannot be connected to a PivotTable at all
Timelines are required before any PivotTable can be created
questions.explain: A Timeline is purpose-built for date fields: instead of one button per date, it offers a range slider and a Years/Quarters/Months/Days zoom level, which scales to years of data.

questions.q: What does the zoom level dropdown on a Timeline control let you do?
options: Switch the granularity of the date filter, such as between Years, Quarters, Months, and Days
Change the color scheme of the Timeline
Convert the Timeline into a regular slicer
Zoom into the underlying worksheet's cell contents
questions.explain: The Timeline's corner dropdown switches its level of granularity, letting the same control filter broadly by year or precisely by day.

questions.q: What is required for a single slicer or Timeline to filter more than one PivotTable at once?
options: The PivotTables must share the same underlying data source, and be connected via Report Connections
The PivotTables must be on the same worksheet, regardless of data source
Nothing — every slicer automatically filters every PivotTable in the workbook
The PivotTables must each have their own separate slicer; connecting one to many is not possible
questions.explain: Slicers and Timelines can be connected to multiple PivotTables that share the same source, letting one click or drag update every connected report at once — exactly what a dashboard-style workbook needs.
